text: You could lose your savings to 7 scams, but only one of them almost nobody spots. I ran it. Which?
I'm Lenny. Ex-scammer. These days I take my old tricks apart, so they stop working on you.
Seven scams. The exact messages. And the one tell that gives each one away. Number seven is last, and it costs the most.
Your parcel could not be delivered. Update your address here.
Here's the trick. You send it to thousands of people at once. Somebody is always waiting for a parcel.
They tap the link, and the page looks exactly like the courier. Logo, colours, tracking number.
It asks for a tiny redelivery fee. A couple of dollars. Nobody thinks twice.
But I never wanted the two dollars. I wanted the card number you just typed in.
The tell is the link. Real couriers don't send you to a random domain with extra words and numbers in it.
Waiting for a parcel? Open the courier's app yourself. Never the link.
Number two. The bank call. This one was my favourite.
Your phone shows your bank's name. A calm voice says there's a suspicious payment, and they need to verify you.
They know your name. Sometimes the last digits of your card. Feels real, right?
Caller ID can be faked. The name on your screen proves nothing. And those details? Old data leaks. Not your bank.
Then comes the ask. Read me the code we just texted you. That code is the key to your account.
So say this. I'll call you back on the number on my card. A real bank says fine. I used to hang up.
That's two down. Number three gets grandparents every single day. And number seven? Stay with me.
